title: Estimating the burden of imported infectious diseases in a prospective cohort of returning travelers
summary:
Background
Increasing global travel volumes mean that novel pathogens can be quickly introduced into Germany. Since the Frankfurt University Hospital is located directly at the airport, travelers returning from abroad are to be examined in order to better understand the spread of infections.

Research question
The study investigates which infections are most common among returning travelers. It aims to examine whether common rapid tests reliably detect these pathogens and whether long travel routes with multiple transfers increase the risk of infection with multiple pathogens.

Methodology
The study is seeking to recruit up to 1,000 adult volunteers who have symptoms such as fever or cough after traveling outside the EU. Participants will answer questions about their trip and their symptoms. Swabs and, if necessary, blood samples will then be taken. These samples will be examined for pathogens in the laboratory.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
Adults over the age of 18 who are capable of giving consent and who have respiratory symptoms and/or fever and/or new skin rashes after traveling outside Europe.

Return from a trip to destinations outside the European Union.

Symptoms must have started during the trip or no later than 48 hours after return.
Exclusion criteria:
Patients under 18 years of age

Incapacity to give consent (e.g., due to language barriers or cognitive impairments)

Taking oseltamivir/baloxavir since the onset of illness.
